g.text: "description": "Inline test cases to upsert into the suite before running.",
"description": "Servers (by ID) the run connects to. Required when creating a new suite; optional on reruns — when omitted,
the run connects the suite's saved server selection (the set its snapshot references). A rerun of a suite with no saved selection
is rejected with `VALIDATION_ERROR` (`details.reason: \"NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION\"`). Rejected outright for a suite with attached
environments (`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE\"`): the environment supplies a closed set that a server ove
rride cannot change, so accepting one would connect a different set than the run is stamped with.",
"description": "When true, skip per-case upsert and rerun the persisted suite. A bare `suiteId` with no `tests` is always tr
"description": "Optional per-provider model API keys (e.g. `{ \"anthropic\": \"sk-ant-…\" }`). Falls back to your organizati
"description": "The floor a run must clear, as a PERCENT in [0, 100] — 80 means 80%. `minimumPassRatePercent` is the canonic
al spelling (the unit is in the name); `minimumPassRate` is the deprecated alias for it. Send exactly one. THE NAME DISAMBIGUATES
THE UNIT: a value in (0, 1) is accepted on `minimumPassRatePercent`, where it unambiguously means a sub-1% floor the evaluator can
act on, and REJECTED on the bare `minimumPassRate`, where `0.8` cannot be told apart from a fraction sent by mistake and would si
lently make the gate unfailable. Neither field ever reinterprets a value. A per-case `passThreshold` IS a fraction; this suite/run
"description": "A percent in [0, 100]. The whole range is usable, sub-1 values included — the unit is in the field name,
so nothing is ambiguous. Note that the GitHub Checks gate rounds the measured rate to an integer before comparing (to stay in ste
p with the eval UI), so a floor below 0.5 behaves there as if it were 0.5; the platform's own verdict compares unrounded."
